When you renovate a house in Romeoville, the people managing your job are often a few minutes away.

The village is an approachable market for investors. Its original Hampton Park neighborhood is full of modest postwar ranches that suit first-time buyers and renters, while the subdivisions west of Weber Road offer newer two-story homes that attract families. Demand is steady thanks to the warehouses and distribution centers along I-55, Lewis University, and easy access to Chicago and the western suburbs.

We coordinate vetted, licensed contractors for every trade, handle permits with the village, and tie every draw to completed work. Before you write an offer, walk us through the address for a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review. We will estimate the repairs, tighten up the ARV and tell you whether the numbers support your price.
housingStock:
Romeoville was a small village along the Des Plaines River and the Illinois and Michigan Canal until the late 1950s, when the Hampton Park development transformed it into a commuter suburb almost overnight. That history shapes nearly every investor deal in town.

Hampton Park, on the east side of the village, was built rapidly from the late 1950s through the 1960s. Its streets are lined with one-story ranches and some raised ranches and bi-levels, typically compact, with simple rectangular footprints and modest lots. A good share were built without full basements, sitting on slabs or crawlspaces, which affects where mechanicals live and how you add space. Many have been expanded or updated by owners over the decades, so quality varies house to house. Common findings include aluminum or older vinyl siding over original sheathing, replacement windows of mixed age, older electrical panels, galvanized supply lines in the original plumbing, and floor tile or mastic that may contain asbestos.

The 1970s and 1980s added townhome developments, apartment complexes and additional single-family streets around the core.

The biggest wave of new construction came from the 1990s through the 2000s, as subdivisions such as Lakewood Falls, Grand Haven and Wesglen spread west of Weber Road toward Plainfield. These are mostly two-story colonials and larger ranches with full basements, attached garages and HOA covenants. Some sit in the Valley View school district and others in Plainfield's.

For a rehab, the two halves of Romeoville behave very differently. Hampton Park houses need careful evaluation of older systems and limited space, but they renovate predictably once those are understood. Newer western subdivisions are mostly about replacing aging roofs, mechanicals and builder-grade finishes, and about keeping basements dry.

commonIssues.title: Slab and crawlspace limitations
commonIssues.body: Many Hampton Park ranches have no full basement, so the furnace, water heater and laundry share a utility room on the main floor and plumbing runs in or under the slab. That limits layout changes and makes drain repairs more invasive, since a cracked line under a slab means cutting concrete. Before you plan a new bathroom or a kitchen relocation, we confirm the foundation type and how drains are routed so the budget reflects what the house will actually allow.

commonIssues.title: Original plumbing and electrical
commonIssues.body: Hampton Park homes are now well over half a century old, and some still have original galvanized water lines, older cast-iron or clay drain lines and electrical panels that insurers and buyers' inspectors question. Low water pressure, slow drains and limited kitchen circuits are typical complaints. These upgrades are often required to sell or refinance. We test water pressure, inspect visible piping and panels, and price replacements clearly as separate line items so you can see where money is going.

commonIssues.title: Asbestos-era materials
commonIssues.body: Homes built during the late 1950s and 1960s commonly used materials that may contain asbestos, such as vinyl floor tiles, black mastic adhesive, pipe insulation and some siding products. Ripping them out without proper handling is a health hazard and can stall a project. We flag suspect materials during the pre-offer review and, when testing confirms asbestos, include licensed abatement in the scope or recommend encapsulating flooring under new material where that approach is appropriate.

commonIssues.title: Sump systems in western subdivisions
commonIssues.body: Newer homes in Lakewood Falls, Grand Haven and Wesglen rely on sump pumps to keep basements dry in clay soil. Pumps installed when the homes were built are now aging, and many lack battery backups. A single failure during a spring storm can ruin a finished basement. We test every sump system on these houses, check discharge lines and grading, and recommend backups before investing in basement flooring, drywall or furniture staging.

commonIssues.title: Aging roofs and builder-grade finishes
commonIssues.body: Roofs, windows, furnaces and air conditioners in the 1990s and 2000s subdivisions are reaching the end of their service lives, often across whole streets at once. Interiors frequently still have original builder-grade cabinets, laminate counters and worn carpet. These are predictable costs, and they are the first items buyers and appraisers notice. We price them clearly and help you decide which ones to replace before listing or renting and which ones can wait.

investorMarket:
Romeoville's investor activity divides mainly between Hampton Park and the newer subdivisions to the west.

Hampton Park is the core of the village's value-add opportunities. Its ranches and bi-levels sell at prices accessible to first-time buyers, making them good candidates for fix-and-flip projects with practical, durable finishes. They also work well as single-family rentals for warehouse and logistics workers, Lewis University staff and families who want a suburban location with easy I-55 access. BRRRR deals can work here when a house is clearly behind its renovated neighbors.

The subdivisions west of Weber Road attract families looking for newer homes, larger yards and specific school districts. Flips there succeed when a house is visibly dated compared to its neighbors, and the renovation focuses on kitchens, bathrooms, flooring and system replacements. Rentals in these neighborhoods command higher rents but require attention to HOA rules and the costs of maintaining larger homes.

Small multifamily properties are limited in Romeoville. Most rental housing beyond single-family homes is in townhome communities and apartment complexes, so investors seeking 2–4 unit buildings often look to Joliet or Lockport while keeping single-family rentals in the village.

Across the village, Will County property taxes are an important part of the math. Model them on the expected post-renovation value, and check whether a property falls within a special service area.
permits:
Building permits in Romeoville are issued by the Village of Romeoville through its community development and building division. Projects that usually need a permit include roofing, siding, window replacement when openings change, decks and fences, basement finishing, kitchen and bathroom remodels that change plumbing or electrical, water heater and furnace replacement, and any structural or layout changes. Larger projects require plan review, and inspections are scheduled at the rough and final stages.

Because the village is relatively compact and our headquarters is here, Genstone's field managers work with the local building staff regularly. That familiarity helps us anticipate what reviewers will ask for and schedule inspections efficiently.

Many newer subdivisions have homeowners associations with architectural rules covering roofing materials, siding colors, fences and other exterior changes. Some properties may be in floodplain areas near the Des Plaines River, which affects additions and basement work.

Landlords should check with the village about any current rental registration or inspection requirements before leasing a property. Genstone confirms permit, HOA and floodplain questions during scoping so the work starts on the correct path.
climate:
Romeoville's flat terrain and open subdivisions leave homes exposed to wind, especially in winter and during spring and summer storms. Hail and wind damage to roofs and siding are common insurance claims in the area, and older Hampton Park homes with aging roofs can be particularly vulnerable.

Freeze-thaw cycles crack driveways, sidewalks and patios, and can heave stoops at front doors. Concrete work and exterior painting are best scheduled between late spring and early fall.

The heavy clay soil that underlies much of Will County holds water, which is why sump pumps and good grading are so important in homes with basements. On slab homes in Hampton Park, poor drainage can lead to water pooling against the foundation and seeping in at the slab edge.

In winter, we concentrate on interior trades and make sure vacant properties are heated or properly winterized. Being headquartered in the village lets our team check on vacant houses quickly after a cold snap or storm.

We are part of the Genstone Companies, which also include Genstone Realty, Genstone Financial, Genstone Insurance, Genstone Property Management, Genstone Field Services and Title Clearing & Escrow. Local projects benefit from having the management team close by, which makes site visits and quick decisions easier.

faqs.q: What kinds of Romeoville homes do investors renovate most?
faqs.a: Hampton Park ranches and bi-levels from the late 1950s and 1960s are the most common investor properties. They are affordable, appeal to first-time buyers and renters, and renovate predictably once older systems are addressed. Newer homes in western subdivisions such as Lakewood Falls and Grand Haven are also renovated, mostly to replace aging roofs, mechanicals and builder-grade finishes before a sale or lease.

faqs.q: Do you handle Romeoville permits and HOA approvals?
faqs.a: Yes. We prepare and submit permit applications to the Village of Romeoville, schedule inspections and keep records of every approval. For properties in subdivisions with homeowners associations, we review the architectural guidelines and help prepare any required submittals for roofing, siding, fences or other exterior changes. Handling both at the start keeps the project from stalling over a missed approval.

faqs.q: How does payment work with Genstone?
faqs.a: You pay nothing upfront. Construction draws are tied to completed and documented work, and final payment is due only after the project is finished and you approve it. Our estimates include dumpster and debris removal, and lien waivers are provided as contractors are paid. Because our office is local, you are welcome to stop by and review your estimate in person with the estimator who wrote it.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Romeoville, IL | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Romeoville fix and flip renovations from a contractor headquartered in the village: Hampton Park ranches and western subdivision homes, paid in draws.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Romeoville
fix-flip.intro:
Flipping a house in the same village where your contractor is headquartered has real advantages. In Romeoville, Genstone's estimators and field managers know the Hampton Park floor plans by heart, they know which western subdivisions have strict HOA rules, and they can be at your property quickly when a decision needs to be made.

Romeoville flips usually fall into two camps: compact Hampton Park ranches aimed at first-time buyers, and dated two-story homes west of Weber Road aimed at families. Each requires a different scope and finish level. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review evaluates the house, identifies hidden costs and recommends a renovation plan matched to recent sales nearby, so you can make your offer with clear numbers.

sections.body:
Hampton Park ranches are some of the most common flip properties in Romeoville. Their compact size and affordable price points make them attractive to first-time buyers, warehouse and logistics workers, and young families.

Buyers here want clean, updated homes without luxury pricing. A typical flip scope includes a refreshed kitchen with new cabinets or painted existing cabinets, durable counters and stainless appliances, an updated bathroom, luxury vinyl plank flooring throughout, fresh paint, new lighting and updated doors and hardware. A second bathroom or half bath adds value where space allows, though in slab homes it requires planning around drain routes.

Hidden costs often include old galvanized plumbing, outdated electrical panels, asbestos floor tiles and aging roofs. On slab homes, sewer or drain repairs may require cutting concrete. Our pre-offer review identifies these risks early and prices them alongside cosmetic work, which keeps your budget realistic and protects your margin when the buyer's inspector walks through before closing.

sections.h2: Flipping homes west of Weber Road
sections.body:
Lakewood Falls, Grand Haven, Wesglen and nearby subdivisions have two-story colonials and larger ranches built in the 1990s and 2000s. Buyers in these neighborhoods compare homes against listings in Plainfield and Bolingbrook, so expectations are higher.

A successful flip here usually includes an updated kitchen with quartz or granite counters, new backsplash and appliances, refreshed bathrooms with tile showers, new flooring on main levels, modern lighting and neutral paint. A dry, finished lower level helps a western Romeoville listing stand out.

The largest costs in these flips are often roofs, furnaces, air conditioners, water heaters and windows that are reaching the end of their service lives. Sump pumps should be tested and upgraded with battery backups. Exterior repairs may involve siding, gutters and garage doors.

Because many of these homes are in HOAs, we review architectural rules before ordering materials. That avoids costly corrections and ensures the exterior matches what buyers and associations expect.

Being headquartered in Romeoville lets us manage local flips closely. Our field managers can stop by job sites frequently, meet inspectors and answer questions without long drives. That proximity helps keep projects moving, especially when quick decisions are needed about hidden conditions or design choices.

We submit permits to the village promptly after closing, or before if your contract allows access, and schedule inspections in sequence so trades are not waiting. Exterior work such as roofing, siding and concrete is planned for warmer months whenever possible, while interior work continues year-round.

Romeoville's buyer activity tends to rise in spring and summer, as in the rest of the Chicago suburbs. If you buy in winter, we prioritize interior work and line up exterior trades for the first good weather window so the house can list when buyer traffic picks up.

Throughout the project, you receive photos and progress notes tied to each draw. Those records keep you and your lender informed and provide documentation you can share with buyers about what was replaced.

faqs.q: What finish level works best for a Hampton Park flip?
faqs.a: Durable mid-range finishes usually work best. Buyers want clean, updated kitchens and baths, new flooring and fresh paint, but they are price-sensitive. Overbuilding with luxury finishes rarely pays off in this neighborhood. We review recent sales nearby and recommend a finish package that matches what buyers in Hampton Park are actually paying for, then price it against your target ARV.

faqs.q: Can I add a bathroom to a Hampton Park slab ranch?
faqs.a: Often yes, but it requires planning. Slab homes need drain lines cut into the concrete floor, and the new bathroom must connect to the existing sewer line at the correct slope. We evaluate the layout and drain routes during the pre-offer review and price the work accurately, so you know whether the added bathroom makes financial sense for that particular house and its comps.

faqs.q: Can I visit Genstone's office to review my flip estimate?
faqs.a: Yes. Our headquarters is at 1267 Windham Parkway in Romeoville, and investors are welcome to meet with an estimator to review a scope, finish options and draw schedule in person. Many local investors find that helpful when deciding between multiple properties or finish levels. Call (312) 429-2637 to set up a time that works for you. Bring listing photos or your inspection report if you have them.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Romeoville, IL | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR renovations in Romeoville by a contractor headquartered in the village: Hampton Park ranches scoped for the refi appraisal and tough rental use.
brrrr.intro:
Romeoville offers a practical setting for BRRRR investing. Hampton Park ranches are affordable enough to leave room for value-add, and rental demand is supported by the large logistics and industrial employers along I-55, Lewis University and the village's location between Chicago and the outer suburbs. With careful buying and an efficient renovation, these homes can appraise well and rent steadily.

Genstone is headquartered in Romeoville, so we work on these houses constantly. We focus BRRRR budgets on the improvements that appraisers count and the materials that hold up under tenants. Through Genstone Financial, you can explore fix-and-flip loans for the purchase and rehab and DSCR rental loans for the refinance, coordinated with our renovation schedule.

sections.h2: Choosing the right Romeoville BRRRR property
sections.body:
The most common BRRRR targets in Romeoville are Hampton Park ranches and bi-levels that have fallen behind their neighbors in condition. Original kitchens and baths, worn flooring, aging roofs and outdated systems often push their prices below renovated comps, creating the value gap a BRRRR needs.

In the western subdivisions, BRRRR opportunities are less frequent because purchase prices are higher, but dated homes do occasionally sell below market. Those deals require precise budgeting because renovation costs on larger homes add up quickly.

Everything hinges on the refi appraiser seeing a finished, market-ready house. Appraisers will compare your property to other renovated homes nearby, so the rehab must bring it in line with those comps. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review estimates the cost to reach that standard and compares it against recent sales. We are not appraisers, but that comparison helps you judge whether the refinance is likely to return enough capital to keep your strategy moving.

sections.h2: Renovating Hampton Park homes for the refinance
sections.body:
Appraisers value permanent improvements and reliable systems. In a Hampton Park ranch, that typically means an updated kitchen and bathroom, new flooring, replacement windows if needed, a sound roof, and upgraded plumbing, electrical and heating.

Replacing old galvanized water lines improves water pressure and reduces leak risk. Updating the electrical panel and adding circuits in the kitchen and bathroom supports modern appliances and reduces insurance concerns. A new high-efficiency furnace and air conditioner can lower operating costs and appeal to tenants. Asbestos materials should be handled properly if disturbed.

We choose finishes that look clean and current but avoid premium costs that may not translate into higher appraisals. Shaker-style cabinets, quartz or laminate counters, luxury vinyl plank flooring and standard fixtures are common choices.

At the end of the rehab, your field manager hands you a summary listing every permit the village closed out, the new equipment installed and paired before and after photos. Sharing that with the appraiser helps them see improvements that are not obvious from a quick walk-through.

Romeoville tenants include warehouse and logistics workers, healthcare employees, Lewis University staff and families looking for suburban space. Many stay for multiple years when the home is comfortable and well maintained.

Durable materials reduce maintenance and turnover costs. Luxury vinyl plank flooring holds up to daily wear, semi-gloss paint on trim and doors is easy to clean, and solid cabinets resist damage. Bathrooms benefit from tile or solid-surface surrounds and strong ventilation fans to control moisture.

In slab homes, water management focuses on grading and gutters to keep water away from the foundation. In homes with basements, sump pumps with battery backups are essential.

We also recommend replacing aging water heaters and servicing heating systems before tenants move in, since those are frequent causes of emergency calls. Genstone Property Management and Genstone Field Services, both part of the Genstone Companies, can support ongoing management, inspections and turns after the BRRRR is complete, keeping the whole process under one family of companies.

faqs.q: Is Romeoville a good BRRRR market?
faqs.a: It can be, particularly in Hampton Park, where affordable ranches and steady rental demand create opportunities. Success depends on buying homes below their renovated value and renovating efficiently. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review helps you evaluate a specific property and compare the renovation cost against recent sales before committing, which is the single most important step in any BRRRR deal. Since the review happens here at home, turnaround is usually quick.

faqs.q: What upgrades matter most for a Romeoville BRRRR?
faqs.a: Updated kitchens and bathrooms, new flooring, sound roofs and windows, and modern electrical, plumbing and heating systems carry the most weight with appraisers. In Hampton Park homes, replacing old galvanized plumbing and outdated electrical panels is often essential. We focus the budget on those improvements and choose finishes that are durable and attractive without overspending. A Hampton Park ranch with new plumbing, a new panel and a clean kitchen usually appraises better than one with fancy tile and original pipes.

faqs.q: Can the Genstone Companies help after the BRRRR is done?
faqs.a: Yes. Beyond Genstone Construction and Genstone Financial, the Genstone Companies include Genstone Property Management, Genstone Field Services and Genstone Insurance. Field Services can handle inspections, occupied maintenance and turns, and Property Management can manage tenants and leases. Using them is optional, but it can simplify long-term ownership for investors who want fewer vendors to coordinate. All of them are reachable through our Romeoville office.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Romeoville | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Single-family rental renovation in Romeoville from a local HQ: durable Hampton Park ranch upgrades, sump and HOA work in newer homes, tenant-ready turns.
rental-renovation.intro:
Single-family rentals are a big part of Romeoville's housing market. Hampton Park ranches house many working families and employees of the logistics centers along I-55, while larger homes in the western subdivisions attract families who want space and specific school districts. Both segments reward landlords who keep homes in solid condition and respond quickly when something breaks.

Genstone renovates rental homes across Romeoville for individual landlords and institutional owners. Our headquarters is in the village, so our field managers can respond quickly and inspect frequently. We focus on reducing service calls, choosing durable finishes and documenting each project for future turns. Genstone Field Services and Genstone Property Management can extend that support after the renovation is complete.

sections.h2: Common rental problems in Hampton Park
sections.body:
Hampton Park rentals are compact, sturdy homes, but their age shows in predictable ways. Old galvanized plumbing restricts water pressure and can leak at fittings. Older electrical panels and limited circuits trip breakers when tenants run modern appliances. Aging furnaces and water heaters fail during the coldest and hottest weeks. Drain lines under slabs can crack or clog, leading to backups that require cutting concrete to repair.

A rental renovation is the right time to address these issues. We replace galvanized supply lines, upgrade electrical panels and add circuits where needed, install new water heaters and service or replace heating and cooling equipment. Camera inspections of drain and sewer lines help identify problems before tenants experience backups.

Exterior issues, such as aging roofs, failing gutters and poor grading around slab foundations, also cause tenant complaints. Addressing them during the renovation reduces water intrusion and helps keep the home comfortable. The result is fewer emergency calls and more predictable operating costs.

Rentals in Lakewood Falls, Grand Haven and Wesglen are newer and larger, but many now need roof replacements, furnace and air conditioner upgrades, new water heaters and refreshed interiors. Tenants in these neighborhoods expect clean, updated homes comparable to what they could find in Plainfield or Bolingbrook.

We typically replace worn carpet with luxury vinyl plank in main living areas, update kitchen counters and fixtures, refresh bathrooms and paint throughout. Sump pumps get tested and upgraded with battery backups, and downspouts are extended to keep water away from basement walls.

HOA rules are a factor in these subdivisions. Exterior repairs, such as roof replacements, siding work or fence changes, must match association guidelines. We review those rules before ordering materials and help prepare any required submittals.

Keeping newer rental homes in good condition helps attract and retain tenants who stay longer and take better care of the property, which supports more consistent cash flow.

Investors with multiple Romeoville rentals benefit from consistent renovation standards. Using the same flooring, paint colors, fixtures, cabinets and appliances across properties simplifies maintenance and allows vendors to stock common parts.

Genstone can help you establish a standard tailored to Hampton Park and newer subdivision homes or apply one you already use. For Hampton Park, the standard should address plumbing and electrical upgrades and asbestos handling. For newer homes, it should cover equipment replacement schedules, sump systems and HOA compliance.

Turnovers are the best time to maintain these standards. A Romeoville turn from us covers touch-up or full repaint, flooring patches, worn fixtures, an appliance check and a walk around the exterior. We also verify smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, handrails and window operation.

Our local team can schedule turns quickly when leases end, helping reduce vacancy. Every job closes with a photo log and a written list of completed items, giving you a clear record for future inspections, deposit reviews and capital planning across your portfolio.

faqs.q: Can Genstone manage my Romeoville rental after renovation?
faqs.a: Genstone Property Management, part of the Genstone Companies, can manage tenants and leases, and Genstone Field Services can handle inspections, occupied maintenance and turns. Using them is optional, but it keeps renovation, maintenance and management coordinated. Because our headquarters is in Romeoville, the teams involved are close to your property and can respond quickly when issues arise. You can also keep your own manager and use us only for renovation work.

faqs.q: Should I replace old plumbing in a Hampton Park rental?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Galvanized supply lines corrode from the inside, reducing water pressure and eventually leaking. Replacing them during a renovation costs less than repeated emergency repairs and improves tenant satisfaction. We test water pressure and inspect visible piping during the pre-offer or pre-renovation review and recommend replacement when the condition warrants it. In a slab ranch, new lines are often run through the attic or walls rather than under the floor.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with a Romeoville rental renovation?
faqs.a: We warranty our workmanship for one year after completion. That means a fixture we installed that leaks, a door we hung that will not latch or trim that separates because of how it was fastened is ours to fix. Wear from normal living and damage caused by tenants are not part of the warranty. Our completion photos help separate the two when questions come up.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex & 2–4 Unit Renovation in Romeoville | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Small multifamily renovation in and around Romeoville: duplexes and nearby Joliet and Lockport two-flats, shared systems and occupied-unit phasing.
multifamily-renovation.h1: Duplex and Small Multifamily Renovation in Romeoville
multifamily-renovation.intro:
Small multifamily buildings are relatively rare in Romeoville. The village developed mostly as a single-family suburb, and much of its rental housing beyond single-family homes sits in apartment complexes and townhome communities. Duplexes and small 2–4 unit buildings do exist in older parts of town and along a few corridors, but investors often expand their search to neighboring Lockport and Joliet, where older two-flats and converted houses are more common.

Genstone renovates duplexes and small multifamily properties in Romeoville and throughout the surrounding area. From our headquarters in the village, we can evaluate buildings quickly, scope shared systems as building-wide items and phase work around occupied units. If a building near downtown Lockport or Joliet makes more sense than anything for sale in Romeoville, we will say so.

sections.h2: What small multifamily looks like around Romeoville
sections.body:
In Romeoville, the 2–4 unit properties investors encounter are usually side-by-side duplexes or small buildings near older parts of the village, along with townhome units that are sold individually. True two-flats and converted Victorian houses are uncommon here.

Nearby communities offer more options. Lockport's older neighborhoods near the I&M Canal have some converted houses and small multifamily buildings. Joliet's downtown, Cathedral Area and east side have a larger supply of two-flats, duplexes and large homes divided into apartments.

Each building type has its own renovation needs. Duplexes often share a roof and foundation but have separate utilities. Older two-flats share foundations, roofs, sewer lines and sometimes heating. Converted homes may have informal unit divisions that raise legal and safety questions.

Genstone evaluates these buildings as complete structures, identifying shared systems and compliance issues and pricing what it will take to bring each unit to a rentable standard. Being close by makes it easy to compare multiple properties quickly.

In any small multifamily property, the shared systems determine much of the renovation budget. A roof, foundation, sewer line or heating system that serves multiple units affects every tenant when it fails.

In Romeoville-area duplexes, shared roofs and foundations are the most common concerns. Roof replacement should be done in one phase to maintain consistent materials and avoid leaks at the dividing line. Foundations in clay soils can crack or allow water seepage, especially when grading and gutters are poor.

Older buildings in Lockport and Joliet may have shared sewer lines, boilers or electrical services. Separating utilities allows tenants to pay their own costs and can improve cash flow and DSCR loan performance, but it requires permits and coordination with utility providers.

We evaluate these shared systems during the pre-offer review and price options for repair or separation. That helps you understand the true cost of the building and plan the renovation sequence before you buy.

Duplexes in and around the village are often sold with a lease running on one side. Renovating while a unit is occupied requires careful planning to maintain safety, comply with lease obligations and keep rental income flowing.

We begin with shared systems that must be addressed first and schedule shutoffs well ahead of time. Work in the vacant unit is contained to limit dust and noise. If the building was constructed before 1978, lead-safe practices are used when disturbing painted surfaces. Asbestos materials common in mid-century construction are handled appropriately.

Exterior work, including roofing and siding, is typically completed in one phase. Inside, each unit gets its turn when its lease runs out.

Because our headquarters is in Romeoville, our field managers can check on occupied buildings frequently and respond quickly to tenant concerns. We coordinate with you on notices and keep driveways and entries clear. Each phase is documented with photos and progress notes tied to draws, so you always know where the project stands.

faqs.q: Are there many duplexes for sale in Romeoville?
faqs.a: Not many. Romeoville is primarily single-family, with most multifamily housing in apartment complexes and townhome communities. Duplexes and small buildings do come up occasionally. Investors seeking more options often look in Lockport and Joliet, where older two-flats and converted houses are more common. Genstone works throughout this area and can compare renovation scopes across communities. Older Lockport buildings near the canal are a frequent alternative.

faqs.q: Can you evaluate multifamily properties outside Romeoville?
faqs.a: Yes. We regularly evaluate and renovate properties in Joliet, Lockport, Crest Hill, Bolingbrook and other nearby communities. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review is free and can help you compare multiple buildings before committing. Being headquartered in Romeoville lets our estimators reach properties throughout this area quickly, often within a short window of your request. That speed helps when good small buildings attract several offers.

faqs.q: Should I separate utilities in a small multifamily building?
faqs.a: Separating heating and electrical services allows tenants to pay their own utilities, which can improve cash flow and help with DSCR loan underwriting. It requires permits, licensed trades and coordination with utility providers. In some buildings, keeping a shared system and including utilities in rent may make more sense. We price both options so you can decide based on the numbers.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Romeoville, IL | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) certified contractor headquartered in Romeoville: Hampton Park ranch updates, Limited and Standard bids, HUD consultant coordination, draws.
fha-203k.intro:
Romeoville's Hampton Park neighborhood is close to ideal territory for the FHA 203(k) loan. Its ranches are affordable, structurally simple and often in need of exactly the kind of updates the program was designed to fund: kitchens, baths, flooring, roofs, windows and mechanical systems. Buyers who cannot afford both a purchase and a separate renovation can finance both with one mortgage.

Genstone Construction is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor, and our headquarters is right here in Romeoville. We work with buyers, agents and lenders to prepare program-ready bids, coordinate with HUD consultants on Standard loans, obtain permits from the village and complete the renovation through draws tied to inspected work, with no upfront payment from the borrower.

sections.body:
Most Hampton Park ranches and bi-levels fit the Limited 203(k) program. It is designed for non-structural repairs and improvements with a cap of $75,000, which covers many of the updates these homes need.

Typical Limited 203(k) work in Hampton Park includes kitchen and bathroom renovations, new flooring, interior paint, roof replacement, new windows, furnace and air conditioner replacement, water heater replacement and updated plumbing and electrical fixtures. Replacing galvanized supply lines and upgrading electrical panels can also fit within the program.

The Limited program does not allow structural changes. Removing a load-bearing wall to open a kitchen or adding square footage requires the Standard 203(k) instead. Many buyers in Hampton Park can accomplish their goals within the Limited program by focusing on updates rather than layout changes.

We help buyers and agents evaluate properties early so they choose the right loan type before making an offer, avoiding delays later in the process.

sections.h2: When a Romeoville home needs the Standard 203(k)
sections.body:
Some Romeoville homes require the Standard 203(k). That includes properties needing structural repairs, layout changes such as removing load-bearing walls, room additions, or total repairs exceeding the Limited cap. Standard loans start at a $5,000 repair minimum, and a HUD-approved consultant writes up the work and signs off on each draw.

In Hampton Park, Standard loans are often used when buyers want to open kitchen layouts, add a bathroom in a slab home or address foundation and drainage issues. In newer subdivisions, Standard loans may be needed for basement finishing combined with major system replacements or structural repairs.

Genstone's estimators prepare itemized bids that align with the consultant's work write-up. We include permit costs, debris removal and detailed material specifications so the lender can underwrite the loan and the consultant can track progress.

We provide our licensing, insurance and contractor documentation upfront and respond quickly to lender questions, helping keep the transaction on schedule.

sections.h2: Draws and local oversight in Romeoville
sections.body:
Once the 203(k) loan closes, renovation funds are held in escrow and released as work is completed and inspected. Our draw schedule follows the program's process, and no money changes hands with Genstone before work is in place.

We obtain permits from the Village of Romeoville and schedule required inspections. With a Standard loan, each draw waits on the HUD consultant's site visit. On Limited loans, the lender verifies progress according to its procedures.

Because our headquarters is in the village, our field managers can visit Romeoville 203(k) projects frequently and meet consultants or inspectors on short notice. That helps keep draws moving and reduces delays.

If hidden conditions appear during the work, such as damaged drain lines under a slab or deteriorated subfloor beneath old flooring, we document them and provide pricing so the consultant and lender can approve use of the contingency reserve. Lien waivers accompany each payment, and the buyer receives a complete record of permits and inspections at the end.

faqs.q: Are Hampton Park homes good candidates for 203(k) loans?
faqs.a: Many are. Hampton Park ranches and bi-levels are affordable and often need updates that fit within the Limited 203(k) program, such as kitchens, baths, flooring, roofs and mechanical systems. Their simple construction makes renovation costs predictable. If structural changes are needed, the Standard program can be used instead, and we help determine which applies before the offer. Agents in the village often call us during showings.

faqs.q: Can I visit Genstone's office to discuss a 203(k) bid?
faqs.a: Yes. Our headquarters is at 1267 Windham Parkway in Romeoville, and buyers and agents are welcome to meet with our estimators to review a 203(k) bid. Meeting in person can help clarify priorities, discuss finish options and understand how the draw process works before closing. Call (312) 429-2637 to schedule a time that fits the transaction timeline. Lenders are welcome to join by phone.

faqs.q: Do you work with any FHA lender?
faqs.a: We work with FHA lenders that offer 203(k) loans and with HUD-approved consultants on Standard loans. Our bids, documentation and draw requests are prepared in the formats lenders require. As an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor, we are familiar with the program's requirements and can help keep the transaction moving smoothly from contract to final draw. Consultants who work Will County often already know our bid format.

reo-renovation.title: REO & Bank-Owned Renovation in Romeoville | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: REO renovation in Romeoville from a contractor headquartered in the village: fast inspections, slab-home water damage, HOA compliance and documented scopes.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Property Renovation in Romeoville
reo-renovation.intro:
For servicers and asset managers handling bank-owned property in Romeoville, response time matters. A vacant house that sits with a broken pipe, a failed sump pump or an open window can deteriorate quickly. Genstone's headquarters is in the village, so our field managers can reach Romeoville properties faster than almost any other contractor.

We serve mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and Government-Sponsored Enterprises, for whom Genstone is a preferred contractor. In Romeoville, we coordinate licensed local trades, handle village permits and HOA requirements, and provide documentation aligned with asset management reporting from first inspection to final billing.

The same team also covers bank-owned homes in Bolingbrook, Lockport, Crest Hill and Plainfield, so a servicer with several assets in this corner of Will County can work with one contractor and one reporting format across all of them.

sections.body:
Vacant Hampton Park homes face specific risks. Without a basement, the furnace, water heater and plumbing are on the main floor, so a frozen or burst pipe can soak floors, drywall and cabinets directly. Water pooling against slab foundations can seep in at the edges. Aging roofs may leak during storms, and older windows can fail.

In western subdivisions, the most common vacant-home problem is basement flooding from a failed sump pump or power outage. Finished basements absorb water quickly, and mold can develop within days in warm weather. Exterior neglect, such as overgrown lawns and missing maintenance, can trigger HOA violation notices and fines.

Theft and vandalism can occur in any long-vacant property, including removal of appliances and copper.

Genstone documents all conditions during the initial inspection and separates urgent stabilization, such as removing water, drying structures and securing openings, from the full renovation scope. That allows asset managers to approve emergency work immediately while evaluating the overall plan.

The Village of Romeoville enforces property maintenance standards for vacant homes, including lawn maintenance, debris removal and securing openings. Properties in HOA subdivisions must also comply with association rules covering exterior condition and approved materials.

Genstone reviews visible violations, open permits and HOA requirements during scoping. Our renovation plans include required corrections and use materials approved by the association. We help prepare HOA submittals for exterior work such as roofing, siding and fences.

Genstone Field Services offers property preservation, inspections, occupied maintenance and code compliance. Our local presence allows frequent inspections and quick response to problems such as storm damage or break-ins. Regular photo reports keep asset managers informed between visits.

When renovation begins, we obtain permits from the village and schedule inspections, keeping records of each step. Resolving violations and open permits early reduces delays at closing and avoids surprises during the buyer's due diligence. It also shortens the list of conditions a buyer's lender can raise.

The renovation scope depends on how the property will be sold or held. Many Romeoville REO homes are sold to owner-occupants using FHA or conventional loans. Those buyers and their lenders expect functioning heating, plumbing and electrical systems, a roof that keeps water out, safe entries and no deteriorated paint on older homes.

In Hampton Park, typical REO scopes include drying and repairing water damage, replacing damaged flooring and drywall, servicing or replacing mechanical systems, addressing asbestos materials if disturbed, and completing paint and cleaning. In western subdivisions, scopes often focus on basement water damage, sump pump replacement, roof and mechanical repairs, and HOA compliance.

Some REO properties are sold to investors or held as rentals. For those, we focus on durable finishes and system upgrades that reduce maintenance.

Our estimates detail labor, materials and draw schedules, with alternate scopes when disposition is still undecided. Our 203(k) certification also supports sales to buyers using FHA renovation financing. Each Romeoville job closes with final approvals from the village, a photo record and lien waivers from all trades.

faqs.q: How fast can you inspect a Romeoville REO property?
faqs.a: Because our headquarters is in Romeoville, we can usually inspect village properties very quickly after assignment. Initial inspections document conditions with photos, identify urgent stabilization needs and lead to a scope and estimate for asset manager review. Timing still depends on access arrangements, but proximity gives us a clear advantage in responding to emergencies like burst pipes or storm damage.

faqs.q: Can you maintain vacant Romeoville homes until sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone Field Services provides securing, debris removal, lawn maintenance, winterization and periodic inspections with photo reports. Keeping a vacant property maintained helps avoid village citations and HOA fines and prevents further deterioration while disposition decisions are made. Our local team can respond quickly when inspections reveal new problems, such as a broken window or a sump failure. Visit frequency can be set by the asset manager.

faqs.q: Do you provide documentation for asset management reporting?
faqs.a: Yes. Each property has a designated manager who provides scopes, estimates, photo documentation and progress updates in formats suited to asset management systems. Draws are tied to completed work, and lien waivers from every contractor accompany payments. Final billing follows completion and approval. That documentation supports internal reporting, investor reporting and resale due diligence. Questions go to one person who knows the property, not a call center.
